planting.note: Divide established clumps or set out container plants in spring once soil is workable, in well-drained, average to lean soil; this species tolerates harsher winters than most garden catmints.

directions: Siberian catmint is a coarser, more upright relative of the familiar border catmints, forming clumps of toothed, gray-green, mint-scented foliage topped from midsummer into early fall with tall whorled spikes of relatively large lavender-blue flowers. Its exceptional cold hardiness and taller habit make it a useful back-of-border choice where winters are too severe for Nepeta x faassenii selections, and the species sets viable seed unlike many sterile hybrid cultivars. Bees and other pollinators visit the flowers readily, and plants are rarely bothered by deer or rabbits once established. Cut stems back hard after the first flowering flush to encourage fresh growth and a lighter rebloom later in the season.
